result.title: From Visual Affinity to Learning Credit in Multimodal Reinforcement Learning
result.summary: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) improves multimodal reasoning, but uniformly assigning a single response-level advantage to all tokens overlooks the distinct roles of visual observations and subsequent reasoning. Visual affinity alone is insufficient: predictive states may align with both image and prompt-context representations, and upweighting valid visual observations can amplify their negative-advantage updates when later reasoning fails. To address this issue, we propose \textbf{Outcome-Conditioned Visual Credit (OVC)}, a plug-in framework that separates visual-association measurement from token-level credit assignment and is adaptable to policy-optimization methods with uniform response-level advantage allocation. Relative Visual Encoding constructs a context-relative visual coordinate by contrasting each predictive state's affinity to image and prompt-context representations. Outcome-conditioned Evidence Calibration combines this coordinate with uncertainty-scaled predictive features and calibrates their contributions to outcome-discriminative evidence through mean contrasts between positive- and negative-advantage responses, scaled by regularized within-side variation. Visual association thus informs credit through observed outcome differences rather than directly determining update priority. Normalized Credit Allocation conditions the calibrated evidence on the response's advantage sign to produce positive token weights with unit global mean. These detached weights preserve advantage signs while modulating individual token-gradient contributions. OVC reuses existing rollouts without auxiliary reward models, process annotations, or inference-time modules. Instantiated through GSPO-token, OVC retains sequence-level clipping and consistently improves six-benchmark mean accuracy over GSPO across three models, with gains of 1.86-2.39 percentage points.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 OVC 插件式框架，在多模态 RLVR 中把视觉关联度量与 token 级信用分配分离，用相对视觉编码、结果条件证据校准与归一化信用分配，使视觉 token 的梯度贡献由结果差异而非单纯视觉亲和度决定。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接对应「贡献分配与监督」及视觉证据筛选问题：指出视觉亲和度高不等于有用、可能放大负优势更新，可供核查 latent 视觉推理中视觉证据是否被真实使用及训练信号如何归因到视觉状态。
